events.headline: Nasdaq 100 futures jumped ~1.4% Friday as chip stocks (Nvidia, AMD, Intel, Broadcom, Micron, up 3.6%-8.2% premarket) rebounded from Thursday's correction-confirming rout, which Reuters tied to fears that the Democratic midterm sweep would bring tougher AI/data-center regulation; VIX eased from its biggest one-day jump in ~19 months

Oil ticked up off post-midterm lows after fresh reports of ship attacks in the Persian Gulf; a senior Iranian official told Reuters that Washington and Tehran remain far from a deal, and Iran's Supreme Leader rejected the idea that the Democratic midterm sweep would soften US policy -- keeping the Strait of Hormuz conflict live even though markets had priced in de-escalation earlier this week

China's one-year suspension of its expanded October 2025 export controls on rare earths, rare-earth processing equipment and lithium-battery/graphite materials is set to expire Nov. 10, 2026, with no official word yet from the Ministry of Commerce on an extension, narrowing, or lapse -- a near-term supply overhang for materials names

The Fed held its benchmark rate at 3.75%-4% on Oct. 28 (10-2 vote, with two officials dissenting in favor of a hike) and gave no clear signal on December easing; today's October nonfarm payrolls report is the next catalyst that could reignite concerns about prolonged Fed hawkishness
